top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) is a mature, general method: ligand design made a narrow, harsh transformation predictable across hindered, heteroaromatic and base-sensitive substrates, and its adoption in medicinal and process chemistry is documented over 25 years. The mechanism is well understood and the two-name allocation is clean, with two independent groups each developing the catalysts. Targeted protein degradation (P001) is a major concept but its PROTAC branch has no approved drug and the citation joins two lines of work, with Sakamoto and Ciulli priority questions open. The lipid nanoparticle proposal (P002) rests on a contested three-name cut and may be judged formulation rather than new chemistry. A prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Buchwald is on the MIT faculty where I was a postdoc with Masamune, but I have no personal or collaborative tie to either credited name
